aspects.name: Primary-source and paper quality
aspects.feedback: The research relies on official NIST resources, an IETF Standards Track RFC, and canonical JSON Lines documentation; all are appropriate to their claims.

aspects.name: Claim-to-source entailment
aspects.feedback: NIST supports documented tests, requirements, and performance criteria; RFC 9562 supports persistent unique identifiers; JSON Lines supports record-per-line persistence. Course-specific schema, polarity, and read-back choices remain explicitly identified as inferences.

aspects.name: Coverage of planned concepts and failure modes
aspects.feedback: The handoff covers the planned criterion, labels, stable IDs, minimum record, identity checks, and JSONL persistence. It accurately marks US-L01-04 partial and explicitly classifies the plan's both-class check as a bounded course decision rather than unsupported research.

aspects.name: Citation completeness and resolvability
aspects.feedback: All four source URLs resolve, all six claims have source links, and CLM-L01-003 now declares both NIST source records needed by its locator.

aspects.name: Technical accuracy and appropriate qualifications
aspects.feedback: The sources are not overstated: UUIDs are optional, exact field names and label polarity are course choices, and no claim asserts a universal class-balance threshold.

aspects.name: Seminal/recent source balance
aspects.feedback: The current 2023-2025 sources are fit for this narrow standards-and-format handoff, but no seminal evaluation or dataset-quality source complements them.

aspects.name: Builder-ready structured handoff
aspects.feedback: The parseable artifact separates sources, claims, locators, scope, limitations, inference flags, user-story links, coverage, and explicit evidence gaps.

deterministic_checks.method: Supplied deterministic claim/source linkage result and direct locator inspection.
deterministic_checks.expected: Every material claim has at least one resolvable source.

deterministic_checks.method: Supplied deterministic authority result and direct source review.
deterministic_checks.expected: At least 80% of central claims have primary or authoritative support.
deterministic_checks.actual: 6/6 central claims have primary or authoritative support (100%).

deterministic_checks.expected: Duplicate records are identified and the duplicate rate is reported.
Required title, authors, year, source type, URL, and authority note are present.

deterministic_checks.method: Compare claims and coverage with the four approved plan user stories and their acceptance criteria.
deterministic_checks.expected: Planned concepts have adequate evidence or an explicit, correctly bounded evidence gap.
deterministic_checks.actual: US-L01-01 through US-L01-03 are covered. US-L01-04 is correctly partial: identity and persistence checks are researched, while both-class presence is explicitly retained as the approved plan's bounded course decision.

deterministic_checks.method: Supplied JSON parse and revision-assertion results.
deterministic_checks.expected: The artifact parses and declares the assigned context and plan revisions.
deterministic_checks.actual: PASS: JSON parses; EP-01, context revision 3, plan revision 1.1, 4 sources, and 6 claims match the supplied assertions.

deterministic_checks.method: Attempt strict validation against research.schema.json using jsonschema.
deterministic_checks.expected: The schema validator executes against the candidate.
deterministic_checks.actual: NOT RUN because jsonschema is unavailable; this remains disclosed and is not represented as passing.

evidence.observation: Direct review resolved all four URLs. NIST and IETF publish the cited standards, and JSON Lines is the format documentation.
The supplied results report 4 sources, 6 claims, and 100% primary or authoritative support for central claims.

evidence.locator: NIST AI RMF Core Measure 2.1 and 2.3; Valid and Reliable section 3.1
evidence.observation: NIST specifies documentation of test sets, metrics, and TEVV tools, documented performance or assurance criteria under relevant conditions, and validation against requirements for a specific intended use.
RFC 9562 supports persistent, unique identifiers generated without central registration; JSON Lines specifies UTF-8, a valid JSON value per line, and newline termination.
All claims include source links, scopes, limitations, inference flags, and user-story IDs; coverage cleanly distinguishes covered stories from the partial validation story.
US-L01-04 is partial, and the artifact explicitly states that both-class presence is a bounded course decision rather than research evidence.
The revised claim declares SRC-L01-NIST-VALIDITY and SRC-L01-NIST-MEASURE, matching its section 3.1 and Measure 2.3 locator.
Weighted scores total 95 and no observable workflow behavior supports a penalty.

strengths: [EV-SJ-L01-103] The NIST sources directly support the course's explicit-criterion and intended-use framing.
[EV-SJ-L01-107] The remediated CLM-L01-003 locator is fully resolvable from its declared source list.
[EV-SJ-L01-106] The research cleanly separates a plan-owned both-class check from claims supported by external evidence.
qualitative_feedback: Approved. DEF-SJ-L01-001 is remediated by marking US-L01-04 partial and explicitly bounding its both-class presence validation as an approved course decision, not a researched claim. DEF-SJ-L01-002 is remediated because CLM-L01-003 now includes both sources named by its locator. Every hard gate passes; all aspect ratings meet the floor; 95 weighted points minus zero penalties yields approval. The unavailable jsonschema validation is retained as an informational not-run check.
